defects.title: A zero-producer opening has no recovery
defects.evidence: Source-reverified; prior runtime fixture remains applicable because these mechanics are unchanged.
defects.detail: 80 starting Cycles can all be spent on Markets and a link. The 25% starvation floor cannot create Cycles when no producer exists, dismantling grants no salvage, and Continue discards undo.
defects.criterion: Spend all starting Cycles on non-producers, save, Continue, then use a documented recovery action to establish a producing Cycles route without restarting.

defects.title: Infrastructure still bypasses ICE affordability
defects.evidence: Source-reverified; source checks Tools only inside the producer match but charges ICE for every placed node.
defects.detail: Markets/Labs placed on ICE subtract unpaid Tools; a later clamp plus undo can refund that unpaid amount.
defects.criterion: With zero Tools, every paid structure in ICE-1 is rejected without changing balances or undo; valid placement and undo restore the exact paid cost.

defects.title: Severing or rerouting an active sweep still leaves a valid trail
defects.evidence: Source-reverified; the active sweep contains static node IDs and checks current-node existence only.
defects.detail: Deleting the tunnel, disabling its source, or changing the parent does not invalidate the snapshotted next hop.
defects.criterion: For every advertised sever/reroute action, the next simulation tick either cancels the sweep or computes a trace route consistent with the live connection graph.

defects.title: The advance warning already quarantines its target
defects.detail: The six-second 'to impact' warning continually refreshes quarantine to 1.5 seconds. Production is interrupted during the promised preparation interval.
defects.criterion: During the full warning interval, production and connectivity remain unchanged; quarantine begins only when the visible tracer reaches the target.

defects.title: Crypto laundering shares Intel saturation
defects.evidence: Current source applies _market_price() to every credits output, including Mixer.
defects.detail: The documented reason to diversify is absent: at 1000 Cash both Intel and Crypto conversions return 0.5 Cash. This behavior is confirmed, but the desired Crypto pricing rule is a design decision.
defects.criterion: Adopt and display an explicit Mixer exchange rule; test payouts at 0, 500 and 1000 Cash, and remove any unsupported diversification promise.

defects.title: Intel's advertised six-tile sweep is not its productive area
defects.evidence: INTEL_RANGE=6 is displayed; production uses the generic radius-four coverage calculation.
defects.detail: Phishing and Scraper show 'Sweeps Intel within 6 tiles' even though buildings exclusively at distance 5–6 cannot affect their yield.
defects.criterion: Put identical eligible blocks exclusively inside and outside the displayed boundary; source yield and highlighted coverage must follow the same rule.

defects.title: Hot Trace compounds a supposed global 20% throttle per hop
defects.evidence: Each edge's survival fraction is multiplied by 0.8 and each packet is admitted separately at every edge.
defects.detail: Apart from other loss, a one-hop route retains 80%, a four-hop route 40.96%. The GDD describes a whole-botnet ×0.8 throttle. Longer Proxy backbones are disproportionately penalized.
defects.criterion: Choose per-route or per-hop security loss explicitly; verify one-hop and four-hop delivery ratios against that rule and show the complete route effect.

defects.title: Onion advertises extra reach with the same routing limit
defects.evidence: Every protocol has a 255-cell maximum; the failure hint suggests Onion after reaching that limit.
defects.detail: Onion does reduce per-cell loss but cannot legally route farther than DNS. It can be sold as low-loss distance transport, or given genuinely distinct reach.
defects.criterion: Either a beyond-DNS-limit route succeeds with Onion, or all descriptions identify its actual lower-loss niche and never suggest it fixes a route-length failure.

defects.title: Notoriety changes sweep cadence, not strength
defects.evidence: Notoriety is labeled as setting strength/frequency; warning 6s, quarantine 7s, blackout 4s and Cash sting 25 remain constant.
defects.detail: Treat this as a stale rule/comment unless variable attack strength is deliberately added; do not call fixed strength an implementation bug.
defects.criterion: Two otherwise identical low/high-Notoriety attacks match the documented warning, traversal and impact rule; the UI explains which properties change.

defects.title: 'Run linked structures' counts disabled nodes
defects.evidence: Contract progress checks graph reachability and non-Proxy identity, not enabled state.
defects.detail: An OFF producer/processor counts as running. Define whether the job requests installation, graph connection or active service, then use that same predicate everywhere.
defects.criterion: Enable, disable, quarantine and disconnect each qualifying node; contract progress follows the displayed eligibility rule on the next tick.

defects.title: Advanced Cycles producers reject green residential ground
defects.evidence: Residential has no ZONE_RES entry; advanced producer placement uses only ZONE_RES.
defects.detail: The GDD says any Cycles ground. Select the intended restriction and derive legal district lists from one mapping.
defects.criterion: Package and Cloud placement on each Cycles district either succeeds or gives the same restriction shown in its tooltip and design document.

defects.title: Going quiet cannot stop the active sweep despite the banner
defects.evidence: Trace and Notoriety are read only when no sweep is active; active traversal never reads protocol noise.
defects.detail: Cooling can reduce future charging only; it cannot cancel or slow an existing sweep. This is a different advertised action from cutting the stored trail, but should be grouped under dependable counterplay in the final review.
defects.criterion: The banner distinguishes future-risk cooling from active defense; if 'go quiet' remains an active countermeasure, a reproducible threshold/protocol change must alter the current tracer.

improvements.title: Validate starting-city solvability
improvements.action: Validate a legal positive-net-Cycles bootstrap and an accessible Intel sales route before accepting the generated city; regenerate or provide bounded recovery if none exists.
improvements.criterion: Across 100 fixed seeds, every start can establish a documented first production/sales loop within the starting budget or the explicit recovery rule.
improvements.dependencies: Authoritative placement/routing predicates; economic correctness

improvements.title: Provide a bounded emergency bootstrap
improvements.action: Make the no-producer, no-money state recoverable through an emergency Cycles source or defined salvage; make the action available after Continue.
improvements.criterion: The zero-producer, zero-resource save fixture can recover without restarting; repeatedly invoking recovery cannot increase resources beyond its recovery allowance.
improvements.dependencies: Define recovery grant/salvage rule

improvements.title: Teach power before sales
improvements.action: Replace the first Intel signpost with establish and connect Cycles, verify a reserve, then obtain Intel and make the first sale.
improvements.criterion: An empty fresh start first recommends a viable Cycles route; after stable power it advances to Intel, and never recommends an unaffordable dead-end step.
improvements.dependencies: Recovery rule; operational-state predicate

improvements.title: Preview delivered yield and break-even power
improvements.action: Add predicted coverage, gross output, route-adjusted delivered output, upkeep and reserve impact to producer placement previews.
improvements.criterion: For three fixed layouts, preview values match settled one-minute observed means within a declared tolerance, with startup transit excluded.
improvements.dependencies: Correct load/loss model; authoritative occupancy

improvements.title: Upgrade producers without rebuilding their network
improvements.action: Offer explicit Phish-to-Scraper and eligible Cycles-producer upgrades that retain identity, parent and valid children while previewing the cost difference.
improvements.criterion: One operation changes the producer, preserves legal tunnels/selection and applies the displayed payment exactly; undo restores the prior type and payment.
improvements.dependencies: Define upgrade pricing; graph edit transaction

improvements.title: Make Proxy role changes reversible after undo expires
improvements.action: Provide an explicit Restore Producer action with a clear payment rule instead of making reverse conversion depend on the last 20 undo records.
improvements.criterion: After more than 20 actions and Save/Continue, an eligible Proxy can return to its original production role without replacing connected branches.
improvements.dependencies: Preserve original producer identity; role-change pricing

improvements.title: Show the full Proxy tradeoff
improvements.action: Preview lost producer output, future vision, effective trunk capacity and the actual40% upkeep before conversion; flag converting the only viable Cycles source.
improvements.criterion: For a sole-Cycles-source selection, the preview identifies loss of recovery income; accepted conversion's output/upkeep/vision matches the preview.
improvements.dependencies: Source availability model; complete capacity diagnostics

improvements.title: Share exploitation capacity across overlapping hacks
improvements.action: Prototype target-building capacity shared by same-resource producers; show overlapping coverage so expansion competes with stacking.
improvements.criterion: Adding a second identical collector over exactly the same targets does not double the shared target yield; moving it to fresh targets increases total delivery.
improvements.dependencies: Authoritative block descriptors; measure baseline density variance

improvements.title: Make coverage count relevant targets
improvements.action: Count eligible resource/district buildings for producer coverage rather than all nearby city blocks; preview the eligible blocks.
improvements.criterion: Replacing nearby Cycles buildings with equal-density Intel buildings changes an Intel collector's output according to the displayed eligibility rule.
improvements.dependencies: Authoritative block descriptors; shared coverage rule

improvements.title: Give entry and advanced producers distinct tradeoffs
improvements.action: Measure complete delivered output, capital cost, upkeep, noise and placement flexibility for Phish/Scraper and Nest/Package/Cloud; give each a concrete use case.
improvements.criterion: In three representative layouts, each producer has at least one documented condition where it beats a direct substitute on cost, reliability or yield.
improvements.dependencies: Correct transport accounting; producer upgrade rules

improvements.title: Measure full-chain investment payback
improvements.action: Provide balance fixtures for each advanced chain that include research, fuel, coverage, round-trip transit, route loss and Cash expenditure.
improvements.criterion: For the selected operation length, each intended midgame investment demonstrably repays before the final stage on at least its advertised favorable layout.
improvements.dependencies: Stable economy fixtures; operation milestone definition

improvements.title: Tie sale saturation to market demand
improvements.action: Use sales volume/demand with a displayed recovery rule, or clearly present current Cash-based repricing as the chosen mechanic.
improvements.criterion: Spending or refunding100 Cash leaves the displayed demand price unchanged under a demand-based rule; identical sale histories yield identical demand.
improvements.dependencies: Explicit market model; transaction ledger

improvements.title: Make Crypto's extra chain earn its complexity
improvements.action: Choose a Mixer premium, distinct demand pool or stability benefit and compare it with an equally funded Intel route.
improvements.criterion: At the advertised late-run condition, the full legal Crypto setup offers a measured advantage over reinvesting the same Cash/research in Intel.
improvements.dependencies: Resolve shared saturation mismatch; stable economic fixtures

improvements.title: Reserve scarce converter resources explicitly
improvements.action: Add per-converter priorities and C2 reserve thresholds for Intel/Cycles; never silently allocate scarce stock by construction order.
improvements.criterion: Two equivalent networks built in reverse order allocate inputs identically when their explicit priorities match; a reserve is never crossed by automation.
improvements.dependencies: Operational converter predicate; transaction ledger

improvements.title: Expose stranded processor inputs and sunk fuel
improvements.action: Report requested, arrived, lost and returning processor units separately so the player sees round-trip waste and paid fuel.
improvements.criterion: In a 10-request forced-loss fixture, the inspector accounts for all 10 inputs and every fuel payment without labeling missing outputs as idle production.
improvements.dependencies: Packet provenance; transport event counters

improvements.title: Top up Overclock rather than wasting remaining time
improvements.action: Show remaining boost and price only the added duration, or disable redundant activation until the boost ends.
improvements.criterion: Reactivating with 15 seconds remaining either charges only the defined five-second top-up or is rejected without changing resources.
improvements.dependencies: Choose command renewal rule

improvements.title: Preview Overclock's useful delivered gain
improvements.action: Show nominal extra output, predicted downstream overload, usable extra deliveries and power cost before activating; identify inactive targets.
improvements.criterion: For an OFF or disconnected source, the preview states zero present delivery; for a capacity-limited source it does not promise twice the delivered goods.
improvements.dependencies: Correct route-throughput model; operational-state predicate

improvements.title: Make recurring contracts require new work
improvements.action: Use delivery since acceptance, incremental production or sustained service for recurring jobs; keep possession milestones as explicitly one-time achievements.
improvements.criterion: The initial 80 Cycles cannot satisfy repeatable jobs without new production/delivery; the same goods cannot be paid for twice.
improvements.dependencies: Packet/production cumulative counters; persisted job baseline

improvements.title: Explain contract success and escrow semantics
improvements.action: State whether goods are consumed, reserved or merely checked; identify when progress locks and whether completion survives subsequent spending.
improvements.criterion: A player can predict outcomes of spending required stock before completion and after completion solely from the card's rule text; tests match both cases.
improvements.dependencies: Choose delivery/possession semantics

improvements.title: Retire or decline unaccepted offers
improvements.action: Add Decline/Reroll with a visible cooldown and expire unaccepted offers so three unsuitable cards cannot permanently fill the board.
improvements.criterion: Three unaccepted unreachable jobs are replaced after the declared offer lifetime, and manual decline produces another eligible offer within the stated cooldown.
improvements.dependencies: Eligible-offer generator; persisted cooldown

improvements.title: Set deadlines from feasible delivered capacity
improvements.action: Filter contracts by discovered/unlocked chains and derive deadlines from measured throughput plus travel and recovery margin.
improvements.criterion: A player without Exploits/Tools/Mixer is not offered an unavoidable 90-second Crypto extraction; all generated jobs have a feasible qualifying route in fixtures.
improvements.dependencies: Capability graph; delivery semantics; offered target reachability

improvements.title: Give clients recognizable contract styles
improvements.action: Make the seven client names correspond to a small set of distinct preferences such as quiet extraction, bulk delivery or research service.
improvements.criterion: Across a seeded sample, each client consistently exposes its documented request/reward/risk preference without introducing unannounced penalties.
improvements.dependencies: New-work job semantics; authored contract templates

improvements.title: Introduce sustained-service contracts
improvements.action: Add a job requiring minimum useful delivered flow for a continuous interval, with pause-safe progress and a clearly forgiving interruption rule.
improvements.criterion: A fixture cannot complete by briefly stockpiling goods; maintain the specified flow for the displayed duration, then receive one reward.
improvements.dependencies: Operating-rate counters; saved interval progress

improvements.title: Point contracts at revealed districts
improvements.action: Add named district extraction jobs with packet provenance so expansion has a concrete purpose instead of any-resource bank thresholds.
improvements.criterion: Intel delivered from an untargeted district does not advance the job; packets from the named eligible district do, and the card focuses that district.
improvements.dependencies: Packet origin/provenance; feasible target selection

improvements.title: Prevent finished cards from blocking the offer cadence
improvements.action: Define automatic settlement or a visible completed-jobs tray so completed rewards do not consume every live offer slot.
improvements.criterion: After completing three jobs, the board can present new live offers while those rewards remain safely claimable exactly once after Continue.
improvements.dependencies: Persist job lifecycle and claim state

improvements.title: Reward effort rather than resource denomination alone
improvements.action: Calibrate stock/extraction payouts by setup, marginal delivered value and timing risk; keep milestone RP separately budgeted.
improvements.criterion: In matched feasible jobs, payout per unit of required effective effort falls inside a declared balance band; initial-Cycles possession has no repeatable high payout.
improvements.dependencies: New-work contract semantics; full-chain balance fixtures

improvements.title: Keep Lab research strategically useful beside job rewards
improvements.action: Record RP earned by Labs versus contracts and choose a repeatable RP reward budget that preserves useful Lab deployment.
improvements.criterion: A contract-only route cannot unlock the entire advanced tree earlier than the intended research specialization without doing equivalently demanding work.
improvements.dependencies: Milestone requirements; reward ledger; actual run measurements

improvements.title: Give research branches different operating solutions
improvements.action: Build stealth, bulk and efficiency/laundering branches with equal viable milestone paths; prerequisites should introduce new supply decisions.
improvements.criterion: Two materially different legal research paths can complete the same standard objective; neither requires buying all seven technologies.
improvements.dependencies: Milestone objective; fixed transport rules; branch ROI fixtures

improvements.title: Let a mistaken research purchase be reviewed and reversed
improvements.action: Show the unlock and spend in a confirmation-free inline preview; provide bounded undo before any dependent object or tech is used.
improvements.criterion: A mistaken unused tech purchase can be reversed with exact RP restoration; undo is rejected once a dependent deployment would invalidate the graph.
improvements.dependencies: Research dependency tracking; safe transaction semantics

improvements.title: Provide a bounded late Research sink
improvements.action: After required technology, offer optional efficiency/stealth modules with clear diminishing benefits so a Lab can remain useful.
improvements.criterion: After all seven techs, RP has an optional paid use with a displayed effect, capped or diminishing so repeated purchases cannot invalidate capacity/recovery rules.
improvements.dependencies: Standard-stage goals; module limits; stable economy

improvements.title: Separate active defense from future-risk cooling
improvements.action: Give each defense command a precise label: cancels current trail, changes its route, delays current impact, or reduces next-sweep charge.
improvements.criterion: The active-sweep countermeasure matrix is reproducible for quieting, cutting, rerouting and DDoS; every displayed claim matches its resulting state.
improvements.dependencies: Repair live-trail handling; define countermeasure rules

improvements.title: Expose sweep charge and meaningful arrival time
improvements.action: Show next-sweep charging state, trigger reason, active time to C2 and target; avoid describing only a hop count as urgency.
improvements.criterion: Given an unchanged path, the displayed arrival estimate remains within 0.5 seconds of impact; pause freezes all clocks and estimates.
improvements.dependencies: Stable live trace; traversal clock; threat HUD layout

improvements.title: Target useful noisy operations instead of insertion-order depth
improvements.action: Weight current protocol noise and useful traffic/economic value, with a visible reason and tie-break rule for target selection.
improvements.criterion: An idle deeper decoy does not always absorb attacks aimed at a valuable noisy branch; a fixed seed and state reproduce the selected target.
improvements.dependencies: Traffic contribution counters; separate simulation RNG

improvements.title: Provide a readable recovery interval after defense
improvements.action: Add a minimum post-blackout or successful-defense grace interval before fresh charging, and display it separately from active attack time.
improvements.criterion: An attack cannot start before the stated grace expires; the player can rebuild a minimal damaged connection during that interval under the chosen preset.
improvements.dependencies: Threat persistence; define cooldown semantics

improvements.title: Offer pressure presets that preserve leisurely planning
improvements.action: Expose quiet/standard/intense sweep settings through a shared ruleset, without changing packet/economy clock accidentally.
improvements.criterion: The presets differ only in documented pressure parameters; the same input delivers equal gross resources over equal simulation time in a no-threat fixture.
improvements.dependencies: Shared rules config; saved/versioned preset

improvements.title: Scale threat stakes against meaningful recoverable economics
improvements.action: Test the fixed 25-Cash blackout sting across early/late operations; use bounded relevant lost income or distinct difficulty values if needed.
improvements.criterion: At each tested milestone, one ignored sweep produces the declared economic setback while leaving a documented affordable recovery route.
improvements.dependencies: Recovery rule; difficulty presets; operation milestones

improvements.title: Show quarantine recovery as a local operation
improvements.action: Display quarantine duration and the affected subtree's lost useful output, with a clear return-to-service event.
improvements.criterion: Quarantine a junction: its full affected branch is identifiable, countdown reaches zero accurately, and restored service is announced once.
improvements.dependencies: Operational-state vocabulary; subtree useful-flow counters

improvements.title: Forecast from sustained operations, not reward spikes
improvements.action: Use a recent operating Cash-rate window and the chosen saturation curve for ETA; label purchases/rewards as separate transactions.
improvements.criterion: Claiming 125 Cash does not turn the ongoing factory rate into 125 Cash/s or create a spurious one-second ETA; a steady synthetic sale flow matches its price-model forecast.
improvements.dependencies: Transaction ledger; selected market-pricing rule

improvements.title: Make standard victory a supplied operation
improvements.action: Use capability milestones and a final supplied protected objective; retain 1000-Cash as a deliberate short scenario.
improvements.criterion: A start-tier Intel/Market loop alone cannot complete Standard; at least two documented alternative specializations can complete its supplied final objective.
improvements.dependencies: Stable correctness/recovery; authored objectives; progression save schema

improvements.title: Earn duration through stage decisions, not arbitrary waiting
improvements.action: Replace the unverified 90–120-minute target as a shipping requirement with measured first-sale, useful upgrade, bottleneck-resolution and final-extraction milestones.
improvements.criterion: Pilot runs include at least three upgrades that change the next decision; idle accumulation is measured separately and each long idle interval has an identified design remedy.
improvements.dependencies: Stable legal economy; formative human playtests

improvements.title: Use seed archetypes to change the best strategy
improvements.action: Add a small authored generator profile set such as distributed low-density targets, a compact finance cluster and stealth-sensitive corridors.
improvements.criterion: Across the same three archetypes, at least two different legal opening/backbone strategies win on measured cost or reliability; all profiles pass bootstrap validation.
improvements.dependencies: Shared versioned rules config; seed solvability; balance fixtures

improvements.title: Add one composed recipe before a new resource taxonomy
improvements.action: Prototype a midgame operation combining two existing delivered resources, such as Intel plus Tools, and give it a visible bottleneck/payoff.
improvements.criterion: The new operation requires both inputs, cannot run from a Cash-only stockpile, and introduces a demonstrable allocation decision without adding another always-required grind.
improvements.dependencies: Explicit converter allocation; packet provenance; milestone objective
